quote: existing GET /users array and id order remain
observable: GET /users with no query returns the same bare JSON array of all users in id order as before the change.

observable: GET /users?name=<lowercase text> matches users whose stored name has uppercase letters (query 'alice' finds 'Alice').
GET /users?name=<UPPERCASE text> matches users whose stored name has lowercase letters (query 'ALICE' finds 'Alice').
GET /users?name=<text from the middle or end of a name> matches that user: a substring anywhere in the name, not only a prefix or the whole name.
A query made of regular-expression metacharacters is matched literally: name=.* or name=a.c or name=( returns 200 with an empty array (no error, no wildcard match).
GET /users?name= (empty value) returns 200 with the array of all users in id order.
GET /users?name=<text that matches nobody> returns 200 with an empty JSON array.
GET /users?foo=bar (alone, or alongside name) returns 200 with the same result as without foo.
Filtered results appear in ascending id order (the same relative order as the unfiltered list).
Each filtered record is the complete user record with every field it has in the unfiltered list.
GET /users/<id> returns the same record and status as before; unknown id gives the same error as before.
exclude_reason: Existing behaviour that must remain; spec says existing tests confirm it.

quote: return JSON object with page, size
observable: The object's page field equals the page served (the number requested, or 1 by default).

quote: return JSON object with page, size
observable: The object's size field equals the size used (the number requested, or 10 by default).
The object's total field is the number of matching records over all pages (all users with no name filter; the matches with one), not the number on this page.
The object's pages field is ceil(total / size): 5 matching users with size 2 gives 3.
With pagination and no matching user, pages is 0 (total is 0 and items is empty).
Page p holds the p-th contiguous slice of size records of the ordered matching list: page 2 size 2 holds the 3rd and 4th users.
Records inside items are in ascending id order.
GET /users?size=2 serves page 1 (page field 1, first two users).
GET /users?page=1 serves 10 records per page (size field 10; with more than 10 users items holds 10).
A page beyond the last page returns 200 with an empty items array (not an error, not the last page).
The last page holds the remaining records, fewer than size: 5 users, size 2, page 3 holds exactly 1 record.
With name and pagination together, total, pages and items come from the filtered list: filtering is applied before slicing.

observable: GET /users?page= (empty value) returns HTTP 400.
GET /users?size= (empty value) returns HTTP 400.
GET /users?page=abc (non-numeric text) returns HTTP 400.
GET /users?size=abc (non-numeric text) returns HTTP 400.
GET /users?page=1.5 returns HTTP 400.
GET /users?size=2.5 returns HTTP 400.
GET /users?page=0 returns HTTP 400.
GET /users?page=-1 returns HTTP 400.
GET /users?size=0 returns HTTP 400.
GET /users?size=-1 returns HTTP 400.
GET /users?size=101 returns HTTP 400.
GET /users?size=100 is accepted (200, size field 100).
GET /users?size=1 is accepted (200, one record per page).
GET /users?page=1 is accepted (200, page field 1).
A page value that is not plain decimal digits but parses to a whole number (page=0x1 or page=1e0) returns HTTP 400.
A size value that is not plain decimal digits but parses to a whole number (size=0x2 or size=1e1) returns HTTP 400.
The 400 response has a JSON content type and a JSON body with an error message.
The error message for an invalid page names the page parameter.
The error message for an invalid size names the size parameter.
